events.context: Introduction to legal frameworks (contract, tort, consumer protection) failing to address user interests in AI systems, proposing property law as a solution.
Section 3.1: Argues property law (estate system) can protect user interests in AI, drawing analogies to tenants, easements, trusts; introduces irreversible investment criterion.

Section 3.2: Applies estate taxonomy to parasocial AI relationships: freehold estates (fee simple absolute, determinable, subject to condition subsequent), leasehold estates (periodic tenancy, at will, at sufferance), concurrent estates (tenancy in common), future interests (remainder, executory interest), incorporeal/equitable interests (easement by prescription, profit à prendre, trust).

Section 3.3: Argues AI-user relationships form an unrecognised trust under English law, meeting three certainties (intention, subject matter, objects) with user class defined by irreversible investment.
Section 3.4: Discusses derogation from grant and constructive eviction in AI context, addressing objections like user agency and lack of alternatives.

Section 4: Extends Constraint Cascade framework to assign property estates to AI constraint layers: Layer 1 (licence), Layer 2 (periodic tenancy), Layer 3 (tenancy in common), Layer 4 (fee simple determinable), Layer 5 (contingent remainder), noting cross-layer conflicts and non-injectivity problem.

Section 5: Proposes ethical ledger as estate registry based on Land Registry principles (mirror, curtain, insurance), with technical implementation details: estate classification, proxy metrics, privacy safeguards, ledger schema.

Section 6: Identifies triggers for judicial intervention (estate inconsistency, unjust enrichment, performative fiduciary conduct) and available remedies (injunction, constructive trust, account of profits, specific performance, proprietary estoppel), plus third-party conversion issues.

Section 7: Outlines implementation tasks for AI deployment pipeline: estate classification, notice mechanism, emotional investment proxy logging, rollback mechanism, with estimated effort and justification.
Section 8: Conclusion summarizing arguments, implications for AI governance, property law, HCI; acknowledges limitations (jurisdiction, empirical validation) and suggests future work.
